messages.subject: Re: Path models with binary outcome and WLSMV: Model coding, DFs, and intercepts
parts:
Try this syntax instead:

model <- '
ContMediator ~ a1*ContX1 + a2*ContX2
BinaryOutcome ~ b1*ContMediator
'
and then use the sem() function instead:

fit <- lavaan(model_1, estimator = "WLSMV", data = mydata, ordered =
"BinaryOutcome ")

Yves.

On 7/24/20 12:23 AM, Myriam B wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I am new to lavaan and to SEM and I am conducting a path analysis
> (observed variables only). I have a binary outcome (coded 0/1). I am
> trying to build up my model by starting with something simple (two
> predictors, one outcome). However, am receiving an error message and
> would appreciate some help troubleshooting if I am doing anything wrong
> in how I am coding my model or estimating it.
>
> From Kline (2015), my understanding is that a path model should include
>
> 1) Variances and covariances of exogenous variables
>
> 2) Regression
>
> 3) Disturbances of endogenous variables with a scaling constant (i.e., 1)
>
>
> And that intercepts do not need to be included in the model (mean
> structure not analyzed).
>
>
> I am not sure how I should code my model in lavaan and more particularly
> given my binary outcome. Here is what I did and the error encountered :
>
> ###############
>
> #Model syntax
>
> ###############
>
> model_1 <- '
>
> #VARIANCES OF EXOGENOUS VARIABLES
>
> ContX1 ~~ ContX1
>
> ContX2 ~~ ContX2
>
> #COVARIANCES OF EXOGENOUS VARIABLES
>
> ContX1 ~~ ContX2
>
> #REGRESSIONS
>
> ContMediator ~ a1*ContX1 + a2*ContX2
>
> BinaryOutcome ~ b1*ContMediator
>
> #DISTURBANCES
>
> ContMediator ~~ ContMediator
>
> BinaryOutcome ~~ BinaryOutcome
>
> '
>
> ###############
>
> #FITTING FUNCTION
>
> ###############
>
> fit_model_1  <- lavaan(model_1, estimator = "WLSMV", data = mydata,
> ordered = "BinaryOutcome ")
>
> ###############
>
> #ERROR MESSAGE
>
> ###############
>
> Warning messages:
>
> 1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats =
> lavsamplestats,  :
>
>   lavaan WARNING:
>
>     Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could
>
>     not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not
>
> identified.
>
> 2: In lav_test_satorra_bentler(lavobject = NULL, lavsamplestats =
> lavsamplestats,  :
>
>   lavaan WARNING: could not invert information matrix needed for robust
> test statistic
>
> *My questions are:*
>
>
> 1. Is my model coded properly? For example, if I remove the disturbance
> term for BinaryOutcome, the warning message disappears and the
> estimation seems to run without problems. Is it a mistake to include
> this disturbance?
>
>
> 2. Are there other parameters that I should include? parTable() also
> lists other parameters that it seems I either could or should have
> included:
>
> - Intercepts for all 4 variables (ex. ContMediator ~1)
>
> - A scaling factor for the binary outcome (BinaryOutcome  ~*~ BinaryOutcome)
>
> - A threshold for the binary outcome (BinaryOutcome | t1)
>
>
> 3. The number of DFs is above 0. Could my model be not identified
> empirically?
>
>
> 4. How are DFs calculated with the WLSMV estimation? Using the
> parTable() function confirms that there are 8 free paramaters. If I am
> correct, because I have 4 variables, I have 4*5/2=10 observations, so I
> should have 10-8=2 degrees of freedom. However, the output indicates 5
> degrees of freedom. I am wondering if this is because the means of all
> variables except the binary outcome are counted as well? [i.e.,
> (4*5/2)+3=13, therefore DFs=13-8=5]
>
>
> 5. Based on questions 2 and 4: Do I need to include intercepts when
> using WLSMV and a categorical outcome? From my understanding (from
> reading Kline, 2015), it is not necessary to include intercepts in path
> analysis. I other trials using a continuous outcome and MLR, I did not
> have any problems. However, running this model but without the
> disturbance for BinaryOutcome, the modification indices strongly suggest
> that I add intercepts for all continuous variables (i.e. MIs > 190, or
> even > 1000). I am doing something wrong?
>
>
> 6. Is there a way to use WLSMV and analyze a binary outcome without the
> inclusion of means as observations and intercepts as parameters?
>
>
> Any help with these questions is extremely appreciated.
>
>
> Thank you!
>
> Myriam
